title: Assignment 3:: CLASSIFICATION AND SELECTION OF LOOPS IN C PROGRAMMING
content:
Assignment: Assignment 3:: CLASSIFICATION AND SELECTION OF LOOPS IN C PROGRAMMING

Here  is a structured
assignment for a DSPM class, designed to help students understand not
only the syntax of loops in C, but more importantly how to choose the
appropriate loop for a particular problem.

Topic: Understanding and Selecting for, while, and
do-while Loops in C
Objective

The best loop is not the one that can solve the problem;
the best loop is the one that expresses the logic of the problem most
naturally.

 
The purpose of this assignment is to develop a clear
understanding of different looping constructs in C programming and to help
students identify which type of loop is most suitable for a given problem.

Students should not merely write programs using loops. They
must analyze the nature of a problem and justify why a particular loop
structure is appropriate.

Submit a detail document on the following

1. HOW
MANY TYPES OF LOOPS ARE THERE IN C?
2. Describe the simple decision rules to select loop.

ASSIGNMENT ACTIVITY

Every student must submit at least one original
programming problem based on loops.

The submitted problem must satisfy the following
requirement:

3. Category A: for Loop

Develop a problem where the number of iterations is known in
advance.
4. Category B: while Loop

Develop a problem where the number of iterations cannot be
known beforehand.
5. Category C: do-while Loop

Develop a problem where the task must execute at least once.

6. Category D: Write a program where it is not possible to use any other loop than while loop.
7. Category E: Write a program where it is not possible to use any other loop than do-while loop.

Justification of submission 

Explain why the selected particular loop with respect to the problem is the most suitable choice.

IMPORTANT CHALLENGE
Students should remember the following:
A programming problem can often be solved using more than
one type of loop. However, good programming is not only about making the
program work. It is also about selecting the structure that best represents the
logic of the problem.
Therefore, while preparing the assignment, first understand the nature of repetition.

title: Assignment 2: Create DOS Command list and learn basic implementation
content:
Assignment: Assignment 2: Create DOS Command list and learn basic implementation

1. The objective of this
assignment is to introduce students to basic DOS (Disk Operating System)
commands and develop familiarity with the Command Prompt environment.
Students will also practice creating and managing a simple list using
appropriate commands.

2. Short
Description

Before starting
advanced Data Structures topics, students should become comfortable with basic
command-line operations. In this assignment, students will learn commonly used
DOS commands such as DIR, CD, MD, RD, COPY, DEL, CLS, and TYPE.

Students will create a
folder structure using DOS commands and prepare a simple list of items, such as
student names, subjects, or data-structure topics. The activity will help
students understand how commands are used to create, view, modify, and manage
files and directories.

3. Learn Basic DOS
Commands 

 
  
   

   

  
 

4. Assignment Task

Students are required
to perform the following activities using Command Prompt:

 
Open Command Prompt.
 
Display the current directory using DIR.
 
Create a folder named DS_ASSIGNMENT.
 
Enter the newly created folder.
 
Create a text file named LIST.TXT.
 
Prepare a list containing at least 3
     items. For example: 
 

  
Names of students
  
Data Structure topics
  
Programming languages
  
Books
 

 
Display the contents of the list using the
     TYPE command.
 
Create a copy of the list with a different
     filename.
 
Rename the copied file.
 
Demonstrate at least five different DOS
     commands and record their purpose and output.

5. Submission
Requirements

Students should
submit: A single document file(.docx/pdf)

 
A list of the DOS commands used.
 
The purpose of each command.
 
The commands executed during the activity.
 
Screenshots showing the execution of the
     commands.
 
The final list created using Command
     Prompt.
 
A short conclusion of approximately 5–6
     lines.

6. Expected
Learning Outcome

After completing this
assignment, students should be able to:

 
Understand the basic working environment
     of DOS/Command Prompt.
 
Execute common DOS commands.
 
Create and manage directories and files.
 
Create and display a simple list using the
     command line.
 
Develop basic command-line skills that
     will be useful for programming and Data Structures practical work.

7. Conclusion

This introductory
assignment provides students with hands-on experience in using DOS commands and
managing simple data through the command line. It establishes basic
computer-operation skills before moving toward more advanced Data Structures
concepts and programming exercises.
